full_judgment:
7. The main contention of the defendant-judgment-debtors is that the entire execution proceeding was started behind their back and without any notice to them. The defendants came to know of the execution case on 2.11.95 when they were evicted from the suit property. The entire proceeding is a fraudulent one to grab the property by drawing up a modified decree on 22:8.98 by the trial court in order to save limitation. The modified decree of the High Court was drawn on 22.3.60 and there was no execution proceeding within the period of limitation as prescribed under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The defendants also asserted that the application for partition of the suit property which was filed behind the back and without the knowledge of the defendant is illegal and the executing court has no jurisdiction to partition the suit property in executing the decree for specific performance of contract. 

 10. It is to be stated at the outset that the decree of the trial court as passed in Title Suit No. 4 of 1994 was modified by the High Court of the then East Pakistan on 22.3.60. The decree of the trial court having been modified by the High Court it merged into the decree of the High Court. Hence, the question of drawing up of a modified decree on 9.8.93 in the light of the judgment and decree of the High Court in First Appeal is wholly illegal and without jurisdiction. It is found that the modified decree was passed on 22.3.1960 and to avoid the question of limitation a modified decree was again drawn up by the trial court on 9.8.93 and which is so obvious that it was obtained from a court by fraudulent means. Even if it is admitted that a mistake was committed by the executing court itself even then there are innumerable authorities of this court to hold that any error or wrong committed by the court itself can be corrected in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to secure the ends of justice and to prevent the abuse of process of court. Thus, the execution proceeding is apparently barred under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The plaintiff did not take any steps within three years from the modified decree of the High Court nor did he keep alive the decree by taking steps to execute the decree within 12 years from the date of the final modified decree. Thus in order to avoid the bar of limitation the plaintiff fraudulently got the modified decree drawn up by the trial court. Hence the application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is maintainable in the facts of the present case.
